posts.title: Neocaml 0.11: OxCaml, Indentation Styles, and odoc
posts.description: I’m happy to announce that neocaml 0.11 is out! I never got around to writing about 0.10, which was mostly about neocaml-utop (a utop backend that talks to utop via its native editor protocol), but 0.11 is a different story. posts.title: Neocaml 0.9: A Better REPL, Dune/Opam Completion, and More Robustness
posts.description: It’s been a couple of months since the last neocaml release, and the reason is simple — for a while there I was genuinely out of ideas. Back when I shipped 0.6 I declared (again!) that I was done with new features, and this time I almost meant it. But ideas have a way of creeping back in, and 0.9 turned out to be a meaty release. Here are the highlights.

posts.title: Emacs loves AsciiDoc
posts.description: Regular readers know I have a soft spot for AsciiDoc – I’ve written about it more than once, and it’s the markup behind the documentation of most of my bigger OSS projects (CIDER, nREPL, Projectile, RuboCop).
